# sphinx-autodoc-typehints [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/sphinx-autodoc-typehints?style=flat-square)](https://pypi.org/project/sphinx-autodoc-typehints/) [![Supported Python versions](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/sphinx-autodoc-typehints.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/sphinx-autodoc-typehints/) [![Documentation status](https://readthedocs.org/projects/sphinx-autodoc-typehints/badge/?version=latest)](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/?badge=latest) [![Downloads](https://pepy.tech/badge/sphinx-autodoc-typehints/month)](https://pepy.tech/project/sphinx-autodoc-typehints) [![check](https://github.com/tox-dev/sphinx-autodoc-typehints/actions/workflows/check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tox-dev/sphinx-autodoc-typehints/actions/workflows/check.yaml) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/tox-dev/sphinx-autodoc-typehints/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/tox-dev/sphinx-autodoc-typehints) [![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/16253/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/16253) This [Sphinx](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/) extension reads the [type hints](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html) of the code autodoc documents and writes them into the parameter and return fields, so you state each type once, in the code. It links every part of a type to its documentation, and resolves names your code imports only for type checkers (inside an `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block) or declares in `.pyi` stub files. It also documents `@overload` variants and default values, and types Google and NumPy style docstrings written for napoleon or numpydoc. ```bash pip install sphinx-autodoc-typehints ``` ```python # conf.py: load autodoc first, then this extension extensions = ["sphinx.ext.autodoc", "sphinx_autodoc_typehints"] ``` ## Why not Sphinx's built-in `autodoc_typehints`? Sphinx's [`autodoc_typehints = "description"`](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/extensions/autodoc.html#confval-autodoc_typehints) already moves annotations into the parameter and return fields, links them, and works with napoleon docstrings and type comments. If your annotations resolve at runtime and you use Sphinx fields or napoleon, that setting may be enough.
Show example code and configuration The same `demo.py` below renders differently with each option. It uses `typing-extensions` for `Doc`. Both builds use `.. automodule:: demo` with `:members:`. The left adds `typehints_defaults = "braces"` and `always_document_param_types = True` to the configuration above; the right loads only `sphinx.ext.autodoc` with `autodoc_typehints = "description"`. ```python from __future__ import annotations from typing import Annotated, Literal, NotRequired, TypedDict, Unpack, overload from typing_extensions import Doc class Options(TypedDict): """Optional controls for a request.""" retries: NotRequired[int] trace: NotRequired[bool] @overload def fetch(path: str, *, mode: Literal["text"], **options: Unpack[Options]) -> str: ... @overload def fetch(path: str, *, mode: Literal["bytes"], **options: Unpack[Options]) -> bytes: ... def fetch( path: Annotated[str, Doc("resource path")], *, mode: Literal["text", "bytes"] = "text", **options: Unpack[Options], ) -> str | bytes: """Fetch a resource. :keyword retries: attempts after a failure :keyword trace: log each request """ return "" if mode == "text" else b"" ```
![This extension puts overloads in a field, types the retries and trace keywords, and turns Annotated Doc into a path description. Built-in Sphinx keeps the overloads in signatures and leaves those keyword descriptions untyped.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tox-dev/sphinx-autodoc-typehints/main/docs/_static/sphinx-comparison.png) The [live TypedDict example](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/concepts.html#keyword-arguments-from-a-typeddict) lets you change the configuration and inspect its output. See the examples for each difference: - [Names imported under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/typing.html#type-checking-imports) link to their real module (`decimal.Decimal`, not a bare `Decimal`). - [Types from `.pyi` stubs](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-to.html#pyi-stubs) fill in functions that carry no annotations, such as those of a C extension. - [`**kwargs: Unpack[TypedDict]`](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/typing.html#kwargs-typed-with-unpack) gets keyword fields typed from the `TypedDict` entries. - [`Annotated[..., Doc(...)]`](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/typing.html#doc) puts descriptions from annotations into the parameter fields. - [numpydoc `Parameters` sections](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-to.html#use-with-numpydoc) get types in place, rather than in a second list. - [`@overload` variants](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/typing.html#overload) get an `Overloads` field, and [default values](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how-to.html#show-default-values) appear next to the types. - [`@deprecated` notices](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/typing.html#deprecated), [`@override` links](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/typing.html#override), and [property setter types](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference.html#property-setters) add details beyond parameter types. The [full comparison](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/concepts.html#compared-with-sphinx-s-built-in-type-hints) lists the differences, and the live examples show each module rendered both ways. The [typing features gallery](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/typing.html) shows source and rendered output for each construct. The [documentation](https://sphinx-autodoc-typehints.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) also has a tutorial, how-to guides and the option reference; [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/tox-dev/sphinx-autodoc-typehints/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) explains how to work on the extension.
